newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania says Belgrade strife may shake Balkans.
newsitem.headline: Albania says Belgrade strife may shake Balkans.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha strongly criticised Serbia on Friday and told ethnic Albanians in its Kosovo region they could not stand idly by during protests in Belgrade if they wanted to win their rights.
In some of his harshest comments about Serbia since coming to power four years ago, Berisha described the Belgrade government as savage and anti-Albanian.

"I greet the Belgrade protests first because they are fighting for a just cause, secondly they are protesting against a regime which provoked Europe's biggest postwar conflict and thirdly because they are protesting against a regime which is undoubtedly the most savage and anti-Albanian of all time," he said.

"It used tanks to take away the rights of the (ethnic) Albanians in Kosovo," he added at an end-of-year news conference in reference to a 1989 clampdown by Belgrade which stripped the region of its autonomy.

Berisha said he believed developments in Serbia, where the opposition has staged daily protests to demand recognition of annulled opposition victories in local polls, showed Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic was determined to survive even at the cost of a civil war.
Police equipped with body armour, shields and truncheons cleared the streets in central Belgrade on Thursday and forced demonstrators back into a pedestrian square.

"What do yesterday's developments show, that Milosevic is determined to survive, to provoke a civil war in Serbia which would have regional complications, very dangerous for the peace and stability in the south of the Balkans," Berisha said.

He said Kosovo's two million ethnic Albanians, who outnumber Serbs in the region by nine to one, had even more reasons than the opposition activists in Belgrade to demonstrate to gain the rights and freedoms denied to them.

"It is very clear for the Kosovo people that their freedom and rights will not come as a gift from anyone and their problems will not be solved in Tirana, Belgrade or Washington, London and Paris," he said.
"They are solved and will be solved in Pristina (the Kosovo capital) and the towns and villages of Kosovo."

While stressing that he fully backed a peaceful solution in Kosovo, Berisha noted that he told the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Lisbon this month that in every conflict the Albanian nation would react as a whole.
It was not immediately clear what he meant by the words "react as a whole" but he stressed that internationally-recognised borders must be respected.

"A democratic Serbia, naturally a Serbia that would recognise the national and human rights of the Albanians, would be a friendly Serbia for its neighbours and a factor of peace and stability for the Balkans," he said.
